checks.title: Enforce authentication through effective Conditional Access
checks.statement: Require approved authentication strength and device conditions on actual sign-ins, including privileged and external access.
checks.prerequisites: Read access to Conditional Access and sign-in logs; Graph Identity.SignIns module with Policy.Read.All for the example. Conditional Access requires appropriate Entra licensing. Use designated test identities.
artifacts: Policy JSON including state, targets, exclusions and grant controls
Authentication-method registrations and strength definitions
What If output and real sign-in correlation IDs
steps: Resolve nested group membership and exclusions for standard, admin, guest and emergency identities; inspect enabled versus report-only state.
Run What If for specific resource IDs, platforms, client types and locations. Test Teams dependencies such as Exchange and SharePoint separately.
Using synthetic accounts, attempt allowed and disallowed sign-ins, including a weaker authentication method. Inspect authentication details and Conditional Access results in logs.
Repeat for an excluded group and an unmanaged device; confirm each exception has a narrow purpose and monitoring.
checks.expected: Approved combinations succeed; disallowed combinations are denied or require the configured strength, with matching policy IDs in logs.
checks.limitations: What If is a simulation and does not cover service dependencies. A registration report or successful MFA prompt alone does not demonstrate coverage. Emergency access has a separate assessment.

checks.title: Expire privileged roles and verify approval
checks.statement: Use time-limited privileged access with independent approval where required and remove unnecessary standing assignments.
checks.prerequisites: PIM read access and an appropriately licensed test identity. Role activation changes access: exercise only an approved low-impact test role.
artifacts: Eligible and active role-assignment exports, including role-assignable groups
Role activation policy, approvers and expiry
Request, approval, activation and deactivation audit events
steps: Join users, groups and service principals to active and eligible roles; include inherited Azure resource roles and direct assignments outside PIM.
Compare duration, justification, authentication context and approval rules with the approved role design. Identify approver absence or self-approval paths.
Request a test activation, verify no privilege before approval, approve independently and demonstrate only the intended scope becomes available.
After expiry, obtain a fresh token and verify the privileged operation fails. Confirm assignment and activation events reach monitoring.
checks.expected: No unexplained permanent privilege; time and resource scope match approval; fresh sessions lose access after expiry.
checks.limitations: Entra roles, Azure resource roles and PIM for Groups require separate inspection. Token caching can delay observed revocation.

checks.title: Separate cloud administrative identities
checks.statement: Administer cloud and directory services through dedicated identities and trusted administrative workstations.
checks.prerequisites: Read access to Entra users, roles, sign-ins and Intune device records; directory administrators provide approved AD group exports.
artifacts: Privileged identity register, onPremisesSyncEnabled attribute and assigned services
Administrative device compliance and sign-in device IDs
AD privileged group and logon-right assignments
steps: Match each administrator to separate daily-use and privileged identities; identify synchronised cloud admin accounts and shared identities.
Check that privileged identities are excluded from routine email and web use and use the intended secure administrative devices.
Inspect recent successful administrative sign-ins and correlate device IDs, authentication strength and source with the allowed design.
Test a privileged test identity from an unapproved device and verify denial; check lower-tier systems cannot administer directory infrastructure.
checks.expected: Administrative access uses separate, appropriately scoped identities and approved devices; ordinary sessions do not carry administrative rights.
checks.limitations: Cloud-only identity requirements apply to cloud administration; AD administration still needs appropriately isolated AD identities.

checks.title: Prove emergency tenant access remains usable and monitored
checks.statement: Maintain independent emergency access that survives failure of normal administration and produces an alert whenever used.
checks.prerequisites: Authorised supervised drill with account custodians; read access to account, role and alert settings. Do not disable production authentication to simulate an outage.
artifacts: Emergency account register and custody records
Cloud-only status, authentication methods and Conditional Access exclusions
Drill sign-in, alert delivery and review record
steps: Verify at least two cloud-only emergency accounts with independent phishing-resistant credentials, permanent emergency role assignment and protected custody.
Trace dependencies on federation, phones, approvers and devices; check cleanup and credential expiry cannot remove access unexpectedly.
Perform a supervised sign-in from the designated secure workstation and a harmless authorised administrative read; record the log correlation ID.
Confirm monitoring notifies the responsible team and a reviewer verifies the reason for use; schedule the next drill.
checks.expected: Emergency access works without normal federation or PIM approval dependencies and every use produces a reviewed alert.
checks.limitations: Apply current Microsoft emergency-account guidance deliberately; do not treat these narrowly controlled accounts as ordinary PIM failures or leave unmonitored MFA bypasses.

checks.title: Close legacy authentication and unneeded SMTP AUTH
checks.statement: Prevent password-only legacy sign-in routes from bypassing the organisation’s authentication policy.
checks.prerequisites: Conditional Access reader and Exchange configuration read access; synthetic mailbox with no real messages. Use ExchangeOnlineManagement with rights to the named read cmdlets. A null mailbox override inherits the tenant setting.
artifacts: Legacy-client sign-in report
Exchange tenant and mailbox SMTP AUTH settings
Conditional Access and authentication-policy exports
steps: Enumerate successful legacy-client sign-ins for an agreed period, including non-interactive sign-ins and service accounts.
Review tenant defaults and mailbox exceptions for SMTP AUTH plus authentication policies; record an owner and replacement plan for every exception.
Attempt a benign legacy sign-in with the synthetic mailbox and confirm failure is attributable to policy rather than a bad password or network fault.
Check modern supported application flows still work and monitor new legacy attempts after policy changes.
checks.expected: No unapproved legacy route succeeds; exceptions are explicit and covered by a separately tested design.
checks.limitations: Availability of legacy protocols changes over time. A lack of recent traffic is not proof a route is blocked.
checks.command:
Get-TransportConfig | Select-Object SmtpClientAuthenticationDisabled
Get-CASMailbox -ResultSize Unlimited | Select-Object Identity,SmtpClientAuthenticationDisabled

checks.title: Reconcile departures and access reviews across connected services
checks.statement: Remove unneeded identities and entitlements across cloud, directory and application layers when people leave or change roles.
checks.prerequisites: Read-only HR/contractor joiner-mover-leaver extract, directory and application account exports; pseudonymise personal fields.
artifacts: HR and contractor end dates
Entra/AD enabled state, role and group membership, app assignments
Disablement, token revocation and access-review decision timestamps
steps: Join authoritative staff and contractor populations to cloud-only, synchronised, guest and local application accounts by stable identifiers; list unmatched records.
Sample departures and transfers, compare end times with disablement and entitlement removal, and inspect subsequent successful sign-ins.
For an authorised synthetic departure, verify fresh cloud sign-in, existing-session access and downstream application access are removed as designed.
Trace denied access-review decisions through to actual removal rather than accepting completed review status.
checks.expected: No unexplained orphan access; removals meet the entity’s approved timeframes and connected applications reflect the decision.
checks.limitations: Disabling Entra does not by itself prove every existing application session or local account is revoked.

checks.title: Restrict OAuth consent and review service principals
checks.statement: Approve application permissions and control credentials for applications that can read or change organisational data.
checks.prerequisites: Application and consent-policy read permissions; application owners assist with permissions not visible to the reviewer.
artifacts: App registrations, enterprise applications and owners
Delegated grants, application roles and credential expiry metadata
User-consent policy and administrator consent decisions
steps: Inventory service principals separately from user accounts; identify high-impact application permissions, unused grants, missing owners and unbounded secrets.
Compare user-consent settings and admin workflow with approved permission classifications; include multi-tenant and publisher-verified apps.
Using a benign test application without data access, attempt an unapproved permission request; verify it cannot self-consent and routes to the correct reviewer.
Review recent permission and credential additions, confirm monitored events, and retest removal using a fresh token in the test app.
checks.expected: High-impact grants have explicit approval and owners; unapproved requests fail; credential metadata demonstrates rotation or a secretless design.
checks.limitations: Do not export secret values. Delegated permissions and application permissions have different effective access and require separate reviews.

checks.title: Limit guest invitations and cross-tenant trust
checks.statement: Limit external access to approved partners and keep guest entitlements current.
checks.prerequisites: External identity configuration reader, guest and group export access, and approved partner test accounts.
artifacts: Invitation restrictions and cross-tenant inbound/outbound settings
Guest sponsor, expiry and access reviews
Partner MFA/device trust settings and sign-in evidence
steps: Compare permitted inviters and external domains with the partnership register; include guest-to-guest invitations and existing guests.
Review partner-specific cross-tenant overrides and whether external MFA/device claims are trusted; confirm the partner assurance supporting that trust.
Try invitations and resource access from approved and disallowed partner test identities; distinguish successful invitation from actual resource authorisation.
Expire a test entitlement through the normal workflow and verify access to its Teams and SharePoint resources is removed.
checks.expected: Only approved invitations and entitlements succeed; inherited partner trust and exceptions are documented and tested.
checks.limitations: Domain allowlists alone do not validate the security posture or identity lifecycle of a partner.

checks.title: Validate SPF, DKIM and DMARC through delivery
checks.statement: Authenticate legitimate senders and reject unauthorised use of organisational mail domains.
checks.prerequisites: DNS read access and Exchange reader; controlled internal and external test mailboxes. Obtain sender approval before simulated impersonation tests. Use an authenticated ExchangeOnlineManagement session with read rights for DKIM configuration.
artifacts: Accepted-domain and approved-sender inventory
SPF, DKIM selectors and DMARC DNS records
Raw received headers and DMARC aggregate reports
steps: Reconcile every active, parked and third-party sending domain with DNS policy and ownership; inspect SPF mechanisms, lookup limits and obsolete senders.
Send benign mail through each authorised route and inspect Authentication-Results, DKIM signature and DMARC alignment at an external recipient.
In an approved test environment, send a deliberately unauthorised test message using an owned test domain and verify the expected disposition.
Inspect aggregate reporting and exception handling; confirm forwarding and mailing-list routes are evaluated before changing enforcement.
checks.expected: Legitimate routes authenticate and align; unauthorised test messages receive the intended quarantine/reject action and reporting is reviewed.
checks.limitations: DNS presence alone is insufficient. SCuBA’s US federal reporting address is not a WA reporting destination.

checks.title: Test mail protection scope, precedence and forwarding
checks.statement: Apply effective phishing, attachment and link protection to all intended recipients and prevent unapproved external forwarding.
checks.prerequisites: Read access to threat policies, recipient scopes and Exchange rules. Safe Attachments/Safe Links require suitable licences; use vendor-provided safe test content.
artifacts: Preset/custom policy assignments, precedence and exclusions
Impersonation protection list and allowlists
Outbound forwarding policy, mailbox forwarding and inbox rules
steps: Resolve policy precedence for standard, executive, shared and exception mailboxes; review user/domain impersonation settings and broad allow entries.
Reconcile external forwarding configured in mailbox settings, inbox rules and transport rules with approved cases.
Send safe vendor test messages to the sample mailboxes; retain message trace, policy decision and quarantine results.
Attempt forwarding of a synthetic message to an owned external mailbox and verify the intended block; check security alerts reach an operator.
checks.expected: Each sample receives its intended effective protection; bypasses and forwarding exceptions are justified and monitored.
checks.limitations: Built-in protection, Standard and Strict presets differ. Never use live malware or real sensitive content for testing.

checks.title: Verify SharePoint and OneDrive effective sharing
checks.statement: Restrict sensitive content to intended people and prevent anonymous or unapproved external sharing.
checks.prerequisites: SharePoint configuration and site-permission read access; synthetic documents and approved external test identities. For PowerShell use the SharePoint Online Management Shell with authorised SharePoint/site administration access. Fetch each site by identity: list results can omit security properties.
artifacts: Tenant and per-site sharing settings
Site owners, guests and existing sharing links
Sensitivity-label settings and external sharing audit events
steps: Compare tenant defaults with site-level settings, labels and existing links; include OneDrive, private/shared-channel sites and sites with exceptions.
Use a synthetic sensitive document to test specific-person sharing, anonymous links and an unapproved external domain.
Open the link as the intended guest, another guest and an anonymous browser; verify actual read/edit rights and download behaviour.
Revoke the link or test entitlement and confirm fresh access fails; correlate creation and revocation with audit records.
checks.expected: Only intended identities receive the permitted operations; broad links and stale permissions do not bypass the approved sharing design.
checks.limitations: Changing a default link type is not proof that old links have been removed. Site access and file sensitivity-label protection are separate.

checks.title: Block unapproved cloud downloads from unmanaged devices
checks.statement: Apply the approved access or session restriction to devices that do not meet management and compliance requirements.
checks.prerequisites: Intune and Conditional Access read access; managed compliant, noncompliant and unmanaged test devices; synthetic files.
artifacts: Compliance policy assignments and exclusions
SharePoint limited-access settings and relevant CA policies
Sign-in device details and endpoint/app-protection reports
steps: Check compliance handling for devices without an assigned policy, stale check-ins, exclusions and grace periods; do not equate enrolment with compliance.
Attempt browser viewing, file download, OneDrive sync and supported mobile-app access from each test device state.
Review actual sign-in device claims and session controls; test direct file URLs and application routes within the approved test scope.
Repeat with an approved guest to check whether partner device trust changes the outcome.
checks.expected: Access and data movement follow the approved device-state matrix; unmanaged clients cannot obtain unrestricted copies through alternate routes.
checks.limitations: Web-only access may still permit some formats or functionality. Validate actual behaviour and document platform-specific limitations.

checks.title: Prove DLP enforcement using synthetic sensitive data
checks.statement: Detect and control movement of locally relevant sensitive information across the organisation’s supported workloads.
checks.prerequisites: Purview policy/report read access, appropriate workload licences and an isolated test group; use synthetic Australian identifiers and dummy documents.
artifacts: Sensitive-information types, classifiers and label definitions
DLP policy locations, rule priority, modes, thresholds and exceptions
Test matches, blocked actions, override justifications and alert records
steps: Map the information register to detection types and locations; include Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive, Teams and endpoints where applicable.
Prepare positive and negative samples with known expected matches, including near-miss formats; run simulation to tune false positives.
With an approved test policy in enforcement mode, attempt external email, sharing and endpoint transfer; verify block, notification and permitted override behaviour.
Check the alert contains enough context for investigation without exposing unnecessary personal data; repeat for excluded users and unmanaged routes.
checks.expected: Expected data types are detected and the intended action occurs across each selected location; negative samples remain usable.
checks.limitations: Simulation records matches but does not prove blocking. US SSN/ITIN examples in SCuBA do not define Australian data requirements.

checks.title: Retrieve cloud events and prove retention coverage
checks.statement: Collect attributable cloud security events, retain them for the required period and demonstrate operational review.
checks.prerequisites: Audit search and SIEM read roles, licence inventory and approved retention schedule; no content export beyond the agreed test records. Use Security & Compliance PowerShell with rights to read retention policies. This command does not return default retention policies.
artifacts: Audit and diagnostic settings, connector health and collection filters
Retention policy priority, user licensing and archive configuration
Known event IDs, query results, alerts and investigation tickets
steps: List required event types per workload and principal type, including guests and administrators; trace each source to its monitoring destination.
Generate harmless test events such as a test-file share or approved test-role change; locate actor, target, timestamp and result in source and central logs.
Retrieve a known historical record near the required retention boundary; test archived retrieval and access restrictions separately from interactive search.
Trigger an agreed benign alert and trace delivery, triage and closure. Compare timestamps with the response target and investigate gaps.
checks.expected: Required events are searchable or recoverable for their approved retention period and reach accountable reviewers.
checks.limitations: Retention varies by workload, licence, user type and policy priority. Do not assume SCuBA’s minimum or a tenant default satisfies the entity’s retention obligations.

checks.title: Test external Teams access and meeting boundaries
checks.statement: Limit external interaction, meeting participation and app access to the organisation’s approved collaboration model.
checks.prerequisites: Teams policy read access and test organisers; approved external managed and unmanaged identities. Use MicrosoftTeams PowerShell with an authorised configuration-reading role.
artifacts: External access domains, guest settings and cross-tenant trust
Effective meeting policies and lobby settings
App availability/permission assignments and installed-app inventory
steps: Resolve each sample user’s effective policies, including group and direct assignments; distinguish federation, guest access and shared channels.
Run a synthetic meeting: verify anonymous participants cannot start it, lobby rules work and external participants cannot unexpectedly control the presenter’s desktop.
Test chat initiation from approved, disallowed and unmanaged external identities; check shared-channel access separately.
Attempt installation of an unapproved harmless test app and inspect permissions on an approved one, including access to backing SharePoint files.
checks.expected: Meeting, messaging and application behaviour matches the approved matrix with no unmanaged path around restrictions.
checks.limitations: Tenant defaults do not prove every user’s effective policy. Recording controls and retention depend on business requirements and licences.

checks.title: Constrain Power Platform connectors and public exposure
checks.statement: Keep business data within approved connector combinations, environments and publication channels.
checks.prerequisites: Power Platform and Power BI configuration read access; a dedicated non-production environment containing synthetic data.
artifacts: Environment inventory, owners and security groups
Tenant/environment data policies and connector groups
Public Power Pages sites and Power BI publish-to-web inventory
steps: Identify default, developer, trial and production environments and their data-policy coverage, including exclusions and custom connectors.
Compare business, non-business and blocked connector groups plus endpoint restrictions with approved data flows; examine tenant isolation separately.
In the test environment, attempt a flow combining a business source and disallowed destination and confirm the intended failure.
Review anonymous site/table permissions and publish-to-web links using synthetic content; verify unapproved public disclosure is prevented.
checks.expected: Every environment has the intended restrictions; disallowed connector combinations and public publication cannot expose protected data.
checks.limitations: Connector DLP classifies connectors, not the sensitivity of each payload; combine it with identity, table permissions and content controls.

checks.title: Detect tenant configuration drift and restore a known configuration
checks.statement: Maintain reviewed configuration snapshots and prove that unapproved changes are detected and reversible.
checks.prerequisites: Read-only configuration exports from the relevant services, a versioned baseline, and an isolated test tenant or resource for restoration.
artifacts: Timestamped configuration exports with tenant/resource IDs
Baseline version, approved exceptions and change tickets
Drift report, alert and test restoration comparison
steps: Enumerate configuration surfaces that the export tool covers and those requiring manual capture; include CA, mail protection, sharing, DLP and administrative assignments.
Compare a fresh export with the approved baseline after normalising volatile IDs and timestamps; verify every material delta has a valid change or exception.
Make a benign approved deviation in the isolated test scope and confirm detection, ownership and escalation.
Restore that test configuration using the reviewed procedure; re-export and compare effective behaviour as well as settings.
checks.expected: Material drift is detected and accountable; a known configuration can be restored without losing required exceptions or locking out administration.
checks.limitations: Do not import ASD DSC templates into production as an assessment. Exports may omit secrets and dependencies; a config snapshot is not a content backup.

checks.title: Reconcile cloud resources and endpoint protection coverage
checks.statement: Find resources missing from security management by comparing independent asset populations.
checks.prerequisites: Read access to Azure Resource Graph, Intune, Defender and configuration records; OT owner supplies passive inventory without active scanning.
artifacts: Azure subscription/resource export
Intune and Defender device IDs, last-seen times and onboarding state
Network discovery, server/virtualisation and OT inventory
steps: Build an independent expected population from subscriptions, procurement, virtualisation and network records; record excluded estates and owners.
Join inventory sources by stable IDs and explicitly report missing agents, duplicate devices, stale records and unknown owners.
For sampled missing and stale devices, verify actual operating state with the owner and determine whether security updates and telemetry are received.
Compare coverage denominators before and after remediation; retain unresolved gaps as findings rather than removing assets from the denominator.
checks.expected: Every expected active resource has an accountable owner and an appropriate management/protection path; unexplained coverage gaps are visible.
checks.limitations: Cloud and endpoint tools cannot inventory every OT component. Use passive, vendor-approved verification for safety-critical environments.

checks.title: Demonstrate application-control enforcement
checks.statement: Prevent unapproved executables, libraries and scripts from running in user-writable locations.
checks.prerequisites: Read access to active policy and event logs; approved isolated Windows test device and harmless unsigned sample programs.
artifacts: Deployed App Control policies and managed-installer configuration
Effective policy mode and device coverage
CodeIntegrity/Operational and AppLocker script/MSI events
steps: Compare active policies with the approved baseline, including supplemental policies, signer rules and audit-only settings.
Inspect ACLs of allowed paths and managed-installer trust; check a standard user cannot place unapproved code into a trusted location.
On the test device, attempt benign unsigned executable and script execution from profile, Downloads, Temp and a writable network share; also test an approved business application.
Correlate denied executable loads with Code Integrity event 3077; audit event 3076 alone is not enforcement. Review script/MSI telemetry separately.
checks.expected: Unapproved code is blocked across tested paths while approved workloads function; coverage includes all intended device classes.
checks.limitations: No policy guarantees coverage from a single executable test. Match tests to the selected Essential Eight maturity requirements.

checks.title: Verify Office macro exceptions and enforcement
checks.statement: Permit macros only for approved users and purposes, with protections against internet-sourced or unsafe macro behaviour.
checks.prerequisites: Office policy and endpoint read access; approved isolated test device with harmless macro samples and relevant Office versions.
artifacts: Effective user/computer Office policy and exception-group membership
Trusted locations and publisher trust
Macro-block messages, antivirus inspection and ASR events
steps: Resolve policy conflicts between GPO, Intune and Office cloud policy for standard and approved macro users; inspect user override and trusted-location permissions.
Test a benign internet-marked macro document, an approved signed macro and an unsigned local macro against their expected policies.
Verify an ordinary user cannot remove protection through an editable trust location or local Office setting; include alternate Office applications in scope.
For an approved isolated test, exercise a harmless prohibited child-process or API action and inspect the relevant ASR decision and support impact.
checks.expected: Only approved macro paths function; ordinary users cannot bypass restrictions and prohibited behaviours are logged and blocked.
checks.limitations: Do not execute untrusted documents. Macro-blocking and ASR are different protections; assess both against the selected model level.

checks.title: Verify endpoint attack-surface rules and protection health
checks.statement: Enforce the selected attack-surface reduction rules and maintain healthy endpoint protection.
checks.prerequisites: Defender read access, suitable endpoint licences and an approved isolated device for Microsoft-provided ASR demonstrations.
artifacts: ASR rule IDs/actions and per-rule exclusions
Defender health, signature age, tamper protection and EDR onboarding
Local and central detection/block events
steps: Pair each ASR rule ID with its configured action and compare with the approved baseline; review broad exclusions and audit/warn modes.
Compare endpoint effective settings with central assignment and investigate conflicting policy or stale check-in state.
Run approved safe demonstrations for selected rules, such as an Office child-process scenario, and verify enforcement plus central telemetry.
Check representative servers and workstations for active protection, update health and reporting; do not count a deployed policy as successful coverage.
checks.expected: Applicable rules enforce the intended action; protection is healthy and exceptions are narrow, owned and reviewed.
checks.limitations: Rule support and prerequisites vary. Some ASR rules do not honour general exclusions; use the rule-specific documentation.

checks.title: Verify vulnerability remediation against actual builds
checks.statement: Identify exploitable and unsupported components and verify that remediation reaches the affected assets.
checks.prerequisites: Read access to scanner results, deployment reports and device inventories; authenticated scan permissions limited to approved scope.
artifacts: Asset-to-scan coverage reconciliation
CVE, installed build/version, exposure and exploit-status records
Deployment results, restart state and independent rescan
steps: Reconcile scan targets with inventory, including internet-facing servers, network devices and software outside the main patch manager.
Determine the applicable remediation deadline from the selected source and exposure conditions; separate deployment age from vulnerability publication and detection dates.
For overdue and recently closed items, inspect installed version and pending restart state; rerun a safe authenticated check or scanner verification.
Trace failed/offline devices, superseded patches and unsupported software to owner action; verify compensating controls and residual-risk acceptance.
checks.expected: Remediation is supported by actual version/rescan evidence and coverage is complete; overdue and unsupported items remain visible.
checks.limitations: A successful deployment job or Get-HotFix alone does not establish application and operating-system vulnerability closure.

checks.title: Restrict local administrator password retrieval
checks.statement: Use unique managed local administrator credentials and restrict who can retrieve or rotate them.
checks.prerequisites: LAPS policy and event-log read access, authorised custodian demonstration and approved test endpoint; do not collect passwords in assessment output.
artifacts: LAPS destination, rotation and encryption policy
Password-read/reset delegation and administrative role memberships
Local LAPS operational events and rotation timestamps
steps: Reconcile endpoint inventory with successful password backup and rotation records; include off-network devices and unsupported configurations.
Resolve effective password-read permissions through AD ACLs or Entra roles; review broad delegated groups and stale staff membership.
Have an authorised custodian demonstrate retrieval without displaying or recording the secret, and verify a non-authorised test identity is denied.
Use a scheduled test rotation and confirm backup succeeds and timestamps advance; check access to the local administrator is constrained after use.
checks.expected: Managed devices have current unique credentials; only approved custodians can retrieve them and retrieval/rotation is auditable.
checks.limitations: AD-backed encryption depends on supported functional levels and configuration. A policy assignment without a successful backup is insufficient.

checks.title: Verify credential isolation is running
checks.statement: Run supported credential-isolation protections on administrative and other in-scope endpoints.
checks.prerequisites: Local device inventory and read access to Device Guard WMI/CIM data; review supported edition, hardware and compatibility.
artifacts: Win32_DeviceGuard runtime state
Secure Boot and virtualisation support
Effective policy and application compatibility exceptions
steps: Identify the device population that should run Credential Guard and its approved exceptions.
Read runtime state on sampled devices and distinguish configured settings from a running protected service.
Investigate devices with configuration present but protection inactive; correlate boot, firmware and policy events.
After an approved fix and normal restart, re-query runtime state and verify affected authentication workloads remain usable.
checks.expected: Credential Guard is running where required and every unsupported or excluded device has a documented treatment.
checks.limitations: Credential Guard protects particular secrets; it does not replace administrative separation or prevent every credential attack.

checks.title: Verify encryption and key custody across data paths
checks.platform: Windows / Azure Key Vault / cloud workloads
checks.statement: Protect sensitive data in storage and transit with approved algorithms and controlled key lifecycle.
checks.prerequisites: Read access to storage encryption, TLS configuration, certificate metadata and Key Vault settings. Do not export key material or recovery secrets.
artifacts: Storage/volume encryption state and key identifiers
Certificate expiry, TLS endpoint configuration and key rotation history
Key Vault RBAC, soft-delete/purge protection and recovery procedure
steps: Trace each sensitive data flow through application, database, backup and integration boundaries, identifying where encryption terminates.
Compare actual algorithms and certificate chains with applicable organisational and source requirements; test negotiated protocols on approved endpoints.
Resolve identities able to read secrets, use keys, change policy or purge keys; review broad inherited roles and emergency recovery custody.
In an isolated test vault, demonstrate the approved recovery procedure using a dummy key or secret and confirm unauthorised principals are denied.
checks.expected: Protected data paths use approved cryptography; key access and deletion are constrained and recovery is demonstrated.
checks.limitations: At-rest encryption does not stop an authorised application from returning plaintext. Customer-managed keys are conditional on the organisation’s requirements.

checks.title: Test Azure and hybrid network boundaries
checks.statement: Permit only approved flows between trust zones, management planes and critical services.
checks.prerequisites: Read access to NSGs, routing, firewall and private-endpoint configuration; explicit approval for harmless connection tests between named test hosts.
artifacts: Current flow matrix, subnet and route diagrams
Effective NSG/firewall rules, public IPs and DNS resolution
Connection-test outcomes and flow/security logs
steps: Compare deployed effective rules and routes with the approved flow matrix, including inherited rules, peering and hybrid connectivity.
From approved test hosts in separate zones, test a small named set of allowed and denied connections; record source, destination, port and expected result.
Verify private endpoints resolve and route as intended and that the corresponding public endpoint cannot bypass the restriction.
Check management access and OT jump paths separately; correlate blocked tests with logs and review unused or broad allow rules.
checks.expected: Approved flows work and prohibited paths fail for the intended policy reason, with evidence at the enforcement point.
checks.limitations: Do not scan production OT. A private endpoint does not automatically disable the service’s public access.

checks.title: Demonstrate protected, complete service recovery
checks.statement: Retain independently protected recovery copies and prove a business service can be restored within its agreed recovery targets.
checks.prerequisites: Backup configuration/log reader and service owners; isolated recovery environment and approved restore exercise with no production overwrite.
artifacts: Business RTO/RPO and dependency map
Backup inventory, job history, retention and deletion protections
Restore timestamps, validation results and supplier attendance
steps: Reconcile protected objects with data and service inventories; include identity, application configuration, keys and required SaaS content rather than assuming provider replication is backup.
Inspect backup-admin separation, immutability/soft delete and credential dependencies; verify production operators cannot remove every recovery copy.
Restore a representative complete service in isolation to an agreed consistent point; measure elapsed time and data loss against RTO/RPO.
Have the business owner validate records and functions, then record gaps, recovery dependencies and a retest date.
checks.expected: Copies remain recoverable under the assumed failure scenario and the restored service meets the agreed business targets.
checks.limitations: Retention, recycle bins, version history and replication are not interchangeable with an independently tested backup strategy.

checks.title: Trace a cloud incident from alert to containment and notification
checks.statement: Make a suspected incident actionable with reliable timestamps, evidence, containment and decision records.
checks.prerequisites: Read access to an approved synthetic incident and ticket workflow; legal/reporting owner defines applicable triggers and clocks. Containment drills use test identities only.
artifacts: Incident/alert timestamps, severity and ownership
Evidence-preservation and containment runbooks
Escalation contacts, reporting decision and exercise timeline
steps: Use a benign synthetic alert to verify event ingestion, triage ownership and escalation outside normal business hours.
Reconstruct detection, awareness, triage and reporting-decision timestamps; determine which obligation applies and when its clock begins.
Exercise a test-account containment or isolated host response and verify service dependencies, evidence capture and recovery approval.
Run a tabletop involving the reporting owner and supplier, record missed handoffs and retest corrective actions.
checks.expected: An operator can follow the case end to end and demonstrate timely decisions against the applicable control and reporting requirements.
checks.limitations: Technical timestamps support, but do not decide, statutory reportability. No real regulator notification or production isolation is sent by this assessment.

checks.title: Validate mobile application protection and retirement
checks.statement: Keep organisational information in approved managed applications and remove it when access ends.
checks.prerequisites: Intune read access and an organisation-owned test device or consenting test BYOD enrolment containing synthetic content.
artifacts: App-protection assignments, conditional-launch and data-transfer settings
Device encryption/compliance state and sign-in claims
Selective-wipe or retirement request and device completion status
steps: Compare app-protection policies with assigned users and supported apps; inspect unassigned users, platform differences and conflicting policies.
Attempt copying or saving synthetic organisational content into an unmanaged app and verify the intended restriction.
In an approved test, retire organisational access or issue a selective wipe; verify completion on the device and denial of fresh access.
Check whether offline content persists until reconnection and confirm that personally owned content is treated according to the selected action.
checks.expected: Organisational content follows approved transfer rules and the tested retirement action removes access/content as designed.
checks.limitations: Selective application wipe is not proof of whole-device sanitisation; an offline or lost device may not receive a command.

checks.title: Validate wireless identity and isolation
checks.statement: Authenticate approved devices and separate guest or unknown clients from protected networks.
checks.prerequisites: Wireless/RADIUS configuration reader, approved test clients and a defined connection-test window.
artifacts: SSID-to-network mapping and enterprise authentication configuration
Certificate trust/profile settings and RADIUS/NAC logs
Guest isolation and segmentation test results
steps: Inspect managed client trust settings and whether users can accept an untrusted authentication server certificate.
Use approved test identities and devices to confirm enterprise authentication succeeds only for the intended population.
Connect a test guest/unknown device through its designated network and test only named protected destinations from the approved matrix.
Verify failed authentication and isolation events reach monitoring and certificates can be revoked through the normal lifecycle.
checks.expected: Managed clients validate server identity; unapproved devices cannot reach protected services and guest isolation works.
checks.limitations: Do not set up a rogue access point or intercept production credentials. Use a controlled lab for hostile-network simulation.

checks.title: Make security ownership traceable to tenant and resource configuration
checks.statement: Use technical coverage and exception evidence to support accountable risk decisions.
checks.prerequisites: Read-only resource/tenant inventory, risk register, service criticality and control ownership records.
artifacts: Tenant/subscription and service-owner register
Coverage metrics with named denominators
Configuration exceptions, due dates and risk decisions
steps: Join each critical service to its tenant, subscriptions, data classification and accountable business/technical owners.
Trace a sample of major risk treatments to configuration IDs, coverage reports and dated enforcement tests; identify unsupported assurance claims.
Check expired exceptions and repeat findings against current configuration and escalation records.
Reproduce one management metric from raw read-only exports; check missing devices or users were not omitted from the denominator.
checks.expected: Risk decisions reflect measured implementation and outstanding gaps have accountable owners and review dates.
checks.limitations: Technical exports support governance; they do not replace management judgement or establish statutory applicability.

checks.title: Verify cloud shared responsibilities and supplier access
checks.statement: Confirm provider assurance covers the actual service and that customer controls and vendor access are implemented.
checks.prerequisites: Read access to supplier inventory, assurance reports, service contracts and relevant identity/resource configuration.
artifacts: Assurance report period, scope, exceptions and complementary customer controls
Delegated access, service principals and support-access records
Supplier exit and service-recovery commitments
steps: Map each critical supplier to the actual product, region, data and dependencies used; inspect report scope and coverage period rather than accepting a logo or certificate.
Translate customer responsibilities into named configuration/operating checks and verify a sample in the tenant.
Inspect vendor permissions, support access approval and expiry, including partner delegated roles and app credentials.
Exercise the documented exit process in a test scope, verifying permissions and credentials are removed and required data remains recoverable.
checks.expected: Provider assurance and customer tests cover the used service; supplier access is attributable and can be terminated.
checks.limitations: An assurance report may exclude subservice organisations or periods. Cloud-provider controls do not prove customer tenant settings.

checks.title: Test data access, minimisation and non-production copies
checks.statement: Limit personal information to approved purposes and prevent production data from escaping into less protected environments.
checks.prerequisites: Approved data-flow inventory, read access to labels and application permissions, and synthetic records representing personal data.
artifacts: Data inventory with purpose, location and owner
Application/record-level permission matrix
Test-data masking, retention and request-handling evidence
steps: Trace sampled personal-data fields through collection, application, analytics, exports and backups; identify undocumented copies and external processors.
Attempt access to synthetic records as authorised and unrelated users, including direct API routes; verify record-level restrictions rather than menu visibility.
Inspect non-production refresh procedures and demonstrate that test data is synthetic or appropriately transformed before vendor access.
Walk a synthetic privacy request or breach scenario through search, preservation, authorised disclosure and escalation, retaining decision timestamps.
checks.expected: Only approved identities and purposes access the data; non-production copies and request workflows reflect the approved privacy design.
checks.limitations: Labelling is not automatic access enforcement. Legal retention and deletion decisions remain with the responsible privacy/records owner.

checks.title: Test deployment separation and pipeline security gates
checks.statement: Prevent unreviewed code and unsafe configuration from reaching production while preserving auditable release decisions.
checks.prerequisites: Read-only repository/pipeline settings, threat model and a dedicated test branch/environment; no production bypass tests.
artifacts: Branch protection, service connections and environment approvals
Dependency, secret, static and dynamic scan outputs
Threat-model abuse cases and release/audit records
steps: Trace a production release from commit to build artifact, scan results, approver and deployment identity; check the artifact is the reviewed build.
In the test branch, introduce a harmless known test failure and verify the required gate blocks release; inspect bypass permissions and branch exceptions.
Check service-connection scope and secretless credentials; verify test identities cannot deploy or read secrets in production.
Select a threat-model abuse case such as object-level access control and run an authorised synthetic negative test; confirm remediation and regression evidence.
checks.expected: Required gates fail closed, production access is separated and security defects are retested before closure.
checks.limitations: Tool success does not prove every threat-model case is covered. Scanner severity thresholds and accepted exceptions must be explicit.

checks.title: Turn findings into repeatable negative tests
checks.statement: Demonstrate that controls resist the intended failure or attack scenario and that remediation survives retesting.
checks.prerequisites: Written test scope, named systems and owners, synthetic accounts/data and recovery arrangements for any active test.
artifacts: Control-to-test traceability and expected outcomes
Tool/version, scope, exclusions and raw test output
Finding owner, fix record and independent retest
steps: Select representative normal and exception populations from independent inventories; define the specific action that should be allowed or denied.
Run read-only checks first, then approved benign negative tests; distinguish lack of permission, missing evidence and unsupported tooling from a pass.
For an attacker-style test, agree the route and stop conditions, validate detection and record only the evidence needed to show the control outcome.
After remediation, repeat the same test and a nearby variant; verify the scope and coverage did not shrink to remove the failing case.
checks.expected: Each conclusion is reproducible and tied to observed behaviour; unresolved and untested conditions remain explicit.
checks.limitations: No single scanner or score establishes compliance. Active penetration testing requires its own approved scope.

checks.title: Reconcile screening and training with enabled access
checks.statement: Check that people with access have completed the relevant screening, induction and role-specific security preparation.
checks.prerequisites: Read-only minimised HR/contractor, identity and learning exports; HR confirms screening status without exposing sensitive background records.
artifacts: Account-to-person reconciliation
Screening/induction status and completion timestamps
Role-specific training, simulation follow-up and acknowledgements
steps: Compare enabled human accounts with employee and contractor records; identify access granted before the approved prerequisites were met.
Sample administrators, developers, incident responders and temporary staff for training suited to their actual permissions.
Run an approved benign reporting exercise or inspect recent simulations; verify reported messages reach the correct team and targeted follow-up occurs.
Check expired training, role changes and contractor renewals generate tracked action without relying on incomplete employee-only lists.
checks.expected: Access populations are accounted for and role-specific preparation is demonstrable; overdue cases have owned action.
checks.limitations: These are technical reconciliation checks supporting a people control. No configuration setting proves screening quality or staff competence.

checks.title: Verify device sanitisation and destruction records
checks.statement: Match the disposal method to the media and information sensitivity, and verify that no readable organisational data remains.
checks.prerequisites: Asset and encryption metadata, disposal procedures and a dedicated sacrificial test device; authorised asset custodian observes any destructive action.
artifacts: Device serial/media type, sanitisation method and tool version
Execution result and independent validation
Chain of custody and destruction certificate
steps: Reconcile retired media with asset and data inventories, including spare disks, failed devices and cloud-provider disposal responsibilities.
Check whether the chosen method is supported for that media and sensitivity; verify cryptographic erase assumptions including all key copies.
On an authorised sacrificial device, observe the approved procedure and independent verification; record success or failure by serial number.
For failed or unsuitable media, trace secure custody to destruction and reconcile the certificate with the original asset.
checks.expected: Every retired item has a valid, verified disposition and unresolved failures remain controlled.
checks.limitations: Intune retirement or a queued remote wipe is not proof of sanitisation. WACC supplies no destructive command.

checks.title: Correlate physical access with service protection
checks.statement: Restrict physical access and verify environmental controls supporting critical systems.
checks.prerequisites: Facilities-approved read access to access-control exports, visitor records, maintenance and alert logs; no unauthorised entry or alarm-disabling tests.
artifacts: Badge permissions and staff/contractor status
Door events, visitor sponsorship and review records
Power/environmental alarm and maintenance evidence
steps: Reconcile server-room badge holders with current roles and contracts; identify shared credentials, stale access and unrestricted vendor badges.
Observe an approved test entry and denial, then trace the event to the review/alert process.
Inspect maintenance records and a safe simulation of environmental alert delivery; verify accountable response and service dependencies.
Where a provider operates the facility, inspect assurance scope and exceptions covering the actual location and customer responsibilities.
checks.expected: Physical access is justified and traceable; equipment protection and alert response are evidenced for the locations relied upon.
checks.limitations: Cloud tenant access does not validate datacentre physical controls. Provider evidence and direct facility tests serve different scopes.

checks.title: Check effective password policy and guessing protection
checks.statement: Apply appropriate password and guessing protections without relying on a single default policy.
checks.prerequisites: Read access to domain/fine-grained policy, Entra password protection and application authentication settings; isolated synthetic identities for negative tests.
artifacts: Default and resultant fine-grained password policies
Custom banned-password and smart-lockout configuration
Authentication failure events and approved service-account exceptions
steps: Resolve the effective policy for standard, privileged, service and local application identities; compare length, banned values and recovery paths with applicable requirements.
In an isolated test identity, attempt a known disallowed dummy password and verify rejection without collecting real passwords.
Inspect lockout and risk signals using a small approved test sequence within the agreed limit; confirm monitoring and recovery avoid account denial of service.
Review service-account rotation, ownership and credential storage separately from ordinary user expiration rules.
checks.expected: Resultant policy and application behaviour meet the approved standard; weak test values fail and guessing events are actionable.
checks.limitations: Do not spray passwords or test production user credentials. Cloud and AD password controls differ; one policy export does not cover both.
